FDM takes advantage of the bandwidth of a transmission medium.

The last characteristic is crosstalk.......................
As in any multiplexing system, crosstalk is the interference between the different information sources.
If the carrier frequencies are too close together, or if the transmission medium causes frequency shifts, crosstalk may occur.
In an FDM system, each information source is separated from the others by a band of frequencies called a GUARD BAND.
The guard band is wide enough that the bandwidths of each information source will not interfere with another source.

FDM MULTIPLEXER CIRCUIT
Typical FDM multiplexers have three major circuits. Note that no timing circuits are used.
DISCUSSION
designed to accept four inputs and use sources and FM modulation.
The example multiplexer is designed to accept four inputs and use them to apply FM modulation to a carrier.n.
The basic idea is to generate four different FM signals that are combined by the summing network and are then used to modulate the MAIN carrier.
The operation is as follows. The four input signals are applied to separate VCOs, generating the FM subcarrier.
The operation is as follows. The four input signals are applied to separate VCOs, generating the FM subcarrier.

VCO - A VCO is a Voltage Controlled Oscillator. The oscillator produces an output frequency according to the input voltage. If the applied voltage varies (in this case,by applying an analog input), then output frequency varies....................................................................
DEFINITION
A filter/amplifier is not used in this circuit. If bandwidth limiting were necessary, it would have to be accomplished before applying the signals to the frequency multiplexer.
The center frequency (fis each VCO is set by a variable resistor. Each fc must be different.

NE567 VCOs are used in this case, the same VCO used in the FM lesson. Remember, other VCO chips can be used.
As a review, pin 2 is the input, pin 6 sets the center frequency, and the output is taken from pin 5.
The outputs of the VCOs are then applied to a summing network.
The summing network, usually a capacitor/resistor network, combines the FM signals into one.
The output of the summing network is used to modulate the MAIN carrier.
The MAIN VCO also has its center frequency set by a variable resistor. Its f must be different from the others.
Finally, the combined FM signal is amplified and sent to the transmission medium.

It's put through a limiter to reduce amplitude variations (noise).
The limiter's output is applied to one input of the phase comparator.
Pins 4 and 5 connect to capacitors which act as a filter and pin 2 has a DC voltage applied to control the loop gain (remember, PLL circuits are closed loops.
The output, a DC error voltage that represents the difference between the VCO and phase comparator, is applied to the VCO.
The DC error changes the frequency of the VCO. The center frequency is set by components connected to pins 12 and 13.
The output of the VCO is fed back into the second input of the phase comparator by an external connection of pins 11 and 3.
The circuit forms a closed loop, like all PLL circuits. It uses the input FM signal to produce an error signal. FM demodulate signal.
The error voltage, a demodulated FM signal, is also applied to the retriever circuit..
The retriever circuit removes steady state DC voltages and produces a well defined analog signal.
The analog signal is amplified and output at pin 14 as the demodulated signal..............
Also note that if digital signals are used, the VCO output on pin 9, instead of pin 11, externally connects to the phase comparator input on pin 3.
Also note that if digital signals are used, the VCO output on pin 9, instead of pin 11externally connects to the phase comparator input on pin 3.
And last, the output of the retriever circuit is applied to a schmitt trigger which produces a digital output.
The NE564 PLL circuit operates like the NE565 PLL circuit with the addition of a limiter, retriever and schmitt trigger.
